| [ADR-110](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-110.md) v2 | A postmortem is due when a schema change has been used, a batch of pull requests closes, a bulk filing lands, a decision is revised soon after landing, a process incident is fixed, or the owner asks; triggers count use and sessions, not calendar time, and a starting policy expected to be superseded | The owner asked on 2026-11-20 when to write a postmortem: not for every pull request, but perhaps for batches. Six triggers, measured in use and in working sessions because the record moves at about ten pull requests, one to five hundred entries and two decisions a day: a change to luria.yaml once about 20 entries use it or at the close of the first session that used it; a batch of five or more pull requests in a session, or any stack that had to be folded; a bulk filing of more than about 50 generated entries; a decision revised within the session it landed or the next; a process incident, once fixed; the owner's request. Not routine single filings that go green first time, nor the bot's repairs. The assistant checks the triggers when a batch closes and proposes; the owner decides. Short form for batches and incidents, the full form for schema changes. The owner expects this to be superseded: it is a starting policy, to be revised as postmortems show what is worth reviewing. Rejected: a postmortem per pull request; calendar intervals; leaving it to ad hoc request. | Proposed |

| [ADR-141](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-141.md) | Every long-running or delegated unit of work persists its progress in the repository as it goes, on a branch of its own, so that a stop at any moment loses at most the step in hand | Alternative (a) of two, filed on the owner's request of 2026-11-22 to stop losing work and to consider which decision needs superseding. [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) makes delegated readers push running notes as they read, but it covers readers only. On 2026-11-22 work was lost or put at risk three ways it does not reach: a lead worker's brief said to commit at the end; the assistant's own background sweep of 184 Unfetched works held its results in memory and was stopped at 162 by the time limit, losing the probe details; and the briefs and triage tables lived in the session's scratchpad, which dies with the container. A devlog note of the same morning had already drawn the lesson for filers and nothing carried it out. Decided, superseding [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) and keeping its reader rules: every unit of work that runs past one tool call, delegated or the assistant's own, works on a branch of its own from its first minute; pushes after every step; keeps a PROGRESS file a replacement can resume from; writes computed results per item, append-only and resumable, inside the repository, with checkpoint commits; is given a time limit above twice its estimate and is restructured, not left to run, when its pace says it will not finish; and keeps briefs and working tables in the repository rather than the scratchpad. The measure is that a stop at any moment loses at most the step in hand. The first application is the lead-worker brief moved into the repository as the run-lead skill. The alternative is [ADR-142](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-142.md), which leaves [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) standing. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [ADR-142](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-142.md) | Lead workers and long computations persist their progress as they go, as delegated readers already do, on a branch of their own, so that a stop loses at most the step in hand | Alternative (b) of two, filed on the owner's request of 2026-11-22 to stop losing work. It leaves [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) standing for readers and adds the two kinds of work that lost or risked work that day: lead workers, whose brief said to commit at the end, and long computations, whose results were held in memory until the end. Each pushes after every step from a branch of its own; a computation writes each item's result as it is produced, inside the repository, resumes by skipping what is written, and is checkpointed at least every ten minutes; a background run gets a time limit above twice its estimate and is restructured when its pace says it will not finish; the lead-worker brief moves into the repository as a skill. The alternative is [ADR-141](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-141.md), which supersedes [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) with one general rule. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [ADR-151](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-151.md) | A synthesis states its scope's argument as one argument, not an inventory of its components; an exchange is taken into account by revising the syntheses of the lines it advanced; and a manuscript argues for its reader, with the record's apparatus in its README | At the owner's word of 2026-11-25: "an 'account' of a discussion should not be a play-by play. it should be updating the nucleation record to *take into account* the progress that was made in the conversation. synthesis 'accounts' suffer a same issue. listing items is not a synthesis of them", and "maybe the word choice of 'synthesis' or 'account' is a source of confusion". The scheme had taken "account" in its bookkeeping sense, an itemized statement, and its syntheses had become inventories: each component with its status, voice and a quotation. Now a SYNTHESIS states its scope's argument as one argument, in prose, in the order its steps depend on each other, citing its components where it uses them; the inventory is the data the entries carry and the generated views render, and is not restated. "Account" is kept only in the sense of an explanation. An exchange gets no synthesis of its own: its filing ends by revising the syntheses of the lines it advanced, so that they take its progress into account, and the curation entry keeps the map of turns. A manuscript argues for a reader outside the record, citing codes in parentheses, with standings, voices and provenance in its README. Rejected: renaming the scheme, since its code and entries stay; and keeping the inventory beside the prose, which is a hand-kept projection of what the entries already say ([DP-003](../../../docs/design-principles.md#dp-3)). | Proposed |
